results.message: What did Augustine say about Psalm 137, dashing the little ones against the rock?

voice_event.speaker: lpc
voice_event.text:
Augustine taught what the little ones of Babylon are, and what the Rock is. The little ones are bad desires at the very start, when they first take hold. Babylon is the city of confusion -- everything that draws a person away. The Rock is Christ himself. So when the psalm says to dash the little ones against the rock, it means this: when a desire first rises in you, before it grows strong, take it to Christ and break it there. Augustine wrote: “How shall they repay her? As she has treated us. Let her little ones be choked in their turn. Yes, let her little ones in their turn be dashed, and die. What are the little ones of Babylon? Evil desires at their birth. For some people have to fight with old, deep-rooted cravings. When a craving is born, evil habit has not yet given it strength against you. While it is little, do not let it gain the strength of evil habit. While it is little, dash it. But you fear that, though dashed, it may not die. ‘Dash it against the Rock; and that Rock is Christ.’”

He does not say the psalm has no other sense, and he does not say the desire dies the moment you dash it. He answers the fear that it will not die by saying it must be dashed against the Rock, which is Christ.

names.name: Augustinius of Hippo Regius, presbyter 391, bishop 395/396-430

figures_used.bridge_line: Our bishop at Hippo. The people seized him and brought him to be made a presbyter while he wept. Later they pressed him into the bishop's office over his own refusal. He spent his last days weeping over psalms of penitence, while an army lay outside the walls.

dates.display: converted 386, baptised 387; seized by the congregation at Hippo and ordained presbyter against his own wishes in 391, weeping through it (Possidius, Vita IV); designated coadjutor and consecrated bishop of Hippo by Megalius, primate of Numidia, in 395/396, again amid popular acclamation (Possidius, Vita VIII); died 430, during the Vandal siege of Hippo

confidence.divergence_note: The text field is the NPNF English as printed. Augustine comments on the Latin Psalter, where Psalm 136 ends 'Blessed is he who shall hold and dash thy little ones against the rock'. 'Choked' renders offocentur, 'be smothered', and 'dashed' renders elidantur, 'be struck down'. The closing words echo 1 Corinthians 10:4, which the Latin cites.
